Upon completion, learners will be able to read and understand a company's annual report, including the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement.

Here is the rewritten paragraph:

This course, "Nutrition and Healthy Eating: Evidence-Based Principles," is designed for learners with a basic understanding of human biology and health sciences. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the scientific principles underlying nutrition and healthy eating, including the roles of macronutrients, micronutrients, and phytochemicals in maintaining optimal health. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and case studies, learners will acquire the skills to critically evaluate the scientific evidence supporting various diets and nutritional recommendations, and to apply this knowledge in making informed decisions about their own eating habits and those of their clients or patients. The course will cover topics such as the epidemiology of chronic diseases, the physiology of nutrient metabolism, and the evidence-based guidelines for healthy eating.

query: Public health and epidemiology basics for a non-clinician
expanded_query: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamentals of public health and epidemiology, designed for individuals without a clinical background. Students will develop a solid understanding of the principles of epidemiology, including the measurement of disease frequency and risk, the study of disease distribution and determinants, and the application of epidemiologic methods in public health practice. Topics will include the epidemiologic triangle, disease surveillance, outbreak investigation, and the role of data analysis in informing public health policy and decision-making. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply epidemiologic concepts to real-world scenarios, identify and interpret relevant data, and communicate effectively with public health professionals. (Prerequisites: None; Target duration: 6-8 hours)

expanded_query: This course provides an introduction to the fundamental principles of psychology and mental health, equipping support workers with the knowledge and skills to effectively engage with individuals experiencing mental health issues. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of human development and behavior, as well as a foundation in communication and interpersonal skills. Topics covered include the biological and psychological factors influencing mental health, the major mental health disorders, and the principles of therapeutic relationships and interventions. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify and respond to the mental health needs of service users, and develop a basic understanding of the psychological theories and models that underpin mental health practice. The course is designed to be completed within 12 weeks, with a target duration of 12 hours of study per week.

expanded_query: This course provides foundational knowledge in human anatomy and physiology, specifically designed to prepare students for a nursing program. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of biology and chemistry. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and hands-on activities, students will develop skills in identifying and describing the structure and function of the human body, including the skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems, as well as the circulatory, respiratory, and digestive systems. The course will also cover the principles of homeostasis, cellular respiration, and the nervous and endocrine systems, with a focus on clinical applications relevant to nursing practice.
